statute_title: Operating Under the Influence of Liquor or Drug
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor or any drug or both
Or had a BAC of .08 or higher
mandatory_minimum: 48 hours or 100 hours community service (first); 120 days (second); 1 year (third+)
enhancements: Child under 16 in vehicle (additional charge under § 53-21)
notes: Connecticut uses 'OUI' (Operating Under the Influence). Implied consent under § 14-227b. Refusal results in 45-day license suspension. Lookback period is 10 years. Ignition interlock required for all offenses.

elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
While under the influence or with BAC .08+
No prior OUI convictions within 10 years
mandatory_minimum: 48 hours imprisonment or 100 hours community service; 45-day license suspension; ignition interlock for 1 year
notes: Eligible for the Pretrial Alcohol Education Program (diversionary program) on first offense. Completion results in dismissal.

elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
While under the influence or with BAC .08+
One or more prior OUI convictions within 10 years
mandatory_minimum: 120 days (second, no suspension); 1 year (third+, no suspension)
notes: Second offense: 120-day mandatory minimum (not suspendable). Third+: 1-year mandatory minimum. License revocation: 3 years (second), permanent (third+). Ignition interlock required.

offense_class: Same as alcohol OUI by offense count
penalty_max: Same as alcohol OUI by offense count
fine_max: Same as alcohol OUI by offense count
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
While under the influence of any drug or the combined influence of alcohol and any drug
To a degree that rendered the defendant incapable of safely operating a vehicle
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol OUI by offense count
enhancements: Combined influence of alcohol and drugs
notes: No per se drug limit. Prosecution must show actual impairment from drugs. Drug Recognition Expert (DRE) evaluations frequently used. Same penalty structure as alcohol OUI.

elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
On a public highway recklessly, having regard to the width, traffic, and use of the highway, the intersection of streets, and the weather conditions
notes: Common plea-down from OUI. May include racing on highways (§ 14-224a).

statute_title: Evading Responsibility — Accident Involving Death or Injury
offense_class: Class C Felony (death); Class D Felony (serious physical injury); Class A Misdemeanor (injury); Infraction (property damage)
elements: Defendant was the operator of a motor vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in injury, death, or property damage
Defendant failed to stop and provide identification and render assistance
notes: Connecticut uses 'evading responsibility' rather than 'hit-and-run.' Death-resulting is a Class C Felony with 1-year mandatory minimum.

statute_title: Manslaughter in the Second Degree with a Motor Vehicle (DUI-related)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle while under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs
Recklessly caused the death of another person
notes: Connecticut charges DUI-related vehicular deaths under the manslaughter statute with motor vehicle enhancement. Class C Felony with 1-year mandatory minimum.

statute_title: Manslaughter in the Second Degree with a Motor Vehicle
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
With criminal negligence caused the death of another person
notes: Non-DUI vehicular deaths may be charged as second-degree manslaughter with motor vehicle. May also be charged as misconduct with a motor vehicle (§ 53a-57).

statute_title: Operating While License Suspended or Revoked
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
While license was under suspension or revocation
Defendant had knowledge of the suspension or revocation
notes: Operating on an OUI-related suspension carries a 30-day mandatory minimum. Additional license suspension upon conviction.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (basic); Class C Felony (death or serious injury results)
penalty_max: 1 year (Class A Misdemeanor); 10 years (Class C Felony)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
When signaled to stop by a uniformed police officer
Defendant refused to stop or fled
enhancements: Death or serious physical injury results (Class C Felony)
notes: Basic eluding is a Class A Misdemeanor. If death or serious injury results, elevated to Class C Felony.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Class D Felony (subsequent)
elements: Defendant possessed a controlled substance
Substance is listed in Connecticut's Controlled Substance Act schedules
Possession was without a valid prescription or lawful authority
notes: First-offense simple possession is a Class A Misdemeanor. Subsequent offenses are Class D Felony. Diversionary programs available for first offenders.

statute_title: Possession of Less Than 1.5 Ounces of Cannabis
offense_class: Civil violation (under 1.5 oz.); Class A Misdemeanor (1.5 oz.-4 oz.)
elements: Defendant possessed cannabis
Amount exceeds the legal limit for personal use
notes: Connecticut legalized recreational cannabis in 2021 for adults 21+. Possession of 1.5 oz. or less is legal for adults. Over 1.5 oz. but under 4 oz. is a civil violation or misdemeanor depending on quantity.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Class D Felony (subsequent)
elements: Defendant possessed cocaine
Cocaine is a Schedule II controlled substance in Connecticut
Possession was without lawful authority
notes: First-offense cocaine possession is a Class A Misdemeanor. Drug court and diversionary programs available.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Class D Felony (subsequent)
elements: Defendant possessed methamphetamine
Methamphetamine is a Schedule II controlled substance
Possession was without lawful authority
notes: Same penalty structure as other controlled substance possession. Meth manufacturing carries separate, harsher penalties.

statute_title: Sale of Controlled Substance — Penalty Enhancement for Large Quantities
elements: Defendant sold, manufactured, or possessed with intent to sell
A controlled substance in a quantity meeting trafficking thresholds
Specific weight thresholds vary by substance
enhancements: Sale near a school (§ 21a-278a, 2-year mandatory minimum)
Use of a minor in trafficking
notes: Mandatory minimum of 5 years, not suspendable. Sale near a school adds a 2-year mandatory minimum consecutive.

statute_title: Sale, Possession with Intent to Sell a Controlled Substance
offense_class: Class B Felony (narcotic, hallucinogen, amphetamine); Class C Felony (other controlled substances)
elements: Defendant sold, dispensed, or offered to sell a controlled substance
Or possessed a controlled substance with intent to sell
enhancements: Sale near a school, day care center, or public housing project (§ 21a-278a)
notes: Sale of narcotics/hallucinogens/amphetamines is a Class B Felony. Other controlled substances are Class C Felony.

offense_class: Class B Felony (narcotic/hallucinogen); Class C Felony (other)
elements: Defendant manufactured, compounded, or processed a controlled substance
Or possessed precursors with intent to manufacture
Without lawful authority
notes: Manufacturing is included in the general sale/distribution statute. Methamphetamine manufacturing has specific provisions.

elements: Defendant possessed drug paraphernalia
With intent to use it for a controlled substance
enhancements: Delivery of paraphernalia to a minor
notes: Possession of paraphernalia is a Class C Misdemeanor. Delivery to a minor carries enhanced penalties. Cannabis paraphernalia is legal for adults 21+.

offense_class: Class B Felony (narcotic/hallucinogen/amphetamine); Class C Felony (other)
elements: Defendant possessed a controlled substance
With intent to sell or dispense
Without lawful authority
enhancements: Near a school, day care center, or public housing (§ 21a-278a)
notes: Intent can be inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, cash, and other circumstantial evidence.

elements: Defendant with intent to cause the death of another person caused the death of such person
Or of a third person
enhancements: Aggravating factors (§ 53a-54b) — murder of law enforcement, multiple victims, murder during kidnapping or sexual assault
notes: Connecticut abolished the death penalty in 2012. Maximum is life without parole. Felony murder (§ 53a-54c) applies when death occurs during commission of certain felonies.

elements: Defendant committed or attempted to commit a specified felony
During the commission of such felony, a person other than a participant was killed
The death was caused by the defendant or another participant
notes: Connecticut's felony murder statute serves as its equivalent to second-degree murder. Applies to deaths during robbery, burglary, kidnapping, sexual assault, arson, and escape.

elements: Defendant with intent to cause serious physical injury to another person caused the death of such person
Or under circumstances evincing an extreme indifference to human life, recklessly engaged in conduct creating a grave risk of death and thereby caused the death
Or committed an act intended to cause death under the influence of extreme emotional disturbance
notes: First-degree manslaughter covers heat-of-passion killings (extreme emotional disturbance) and reckless killings showing extreme indifference.

elements: Defendant recklessly caused the death of another person
Defendant was aware of and consciously disregarded a substantial and unjustifiable risk
notes: Second-degree manslaughter covers reckless killings. Less culpable than first-degree (extreme indifference). Class C Felony.

elements: Defendant with intent to cause serious physical injury caused such injury to another person by means of a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument
Or recklessly engaged in conduct creating risk of death and caused serious physical injury
Or caused serious physical injury with extreme indifference to human life
enhancements: Use of a firearm (mandatory additional time)
notes: First-degree assault has a 5-year mandatory minimum. Class B Felony. One of the most serious assault charges in Connecticut.

elements: Defendant with intent to cause physical injury to another person caused such injury
Or recklessly caused physical injury to another person
Or with criminal negligence caused physical injury by means of a deadly weapon
notes: Third-degree assault is the base assault offense. Class A Misdemeanor. Second-degree assault (§ 53a-60) is a Class D Felony.

statute_title: Assault in the Third Degree (Battery equivalent)
elements: Defendant intentionally caused physical injury to another person
notes: Connecticut merged assault and battery into the assault statutes. There is no separate battery offense.

elements: Defendant committed a larceny
Defendant used or threatened the immediate use of physical force upon another person
For the purpose of preventing resistance to the taking or compel the owner to deliver the property
notes: Third-degree robbery is the base offense. Second degree (§ 53a-135) is aided by another or causes injury (Class C Felony). First degree (§ 53a-134) involves a deadly weapon or serious injury (Class B Felony).

elements: Defendant committed a robbery
While armed with a deadly weapon
Or caused serious physical injury to a non-participant
notes: Class B Felony with 5-year mandatory minimum. Armed with a deadly weapon or causing serious injury elevates to first degree.

penalty_max: 25 years (or life if certain aggravating factors)
elements: Defendant abducted another person and restrained such person
With intent to compel a third person to do or refrain from doing something, or to inflict physical injury
Or held for ransom
notes: First-degree kidnapping is a Class A Felony. Second-degree (§ 53a-94) is a Class B Felony involving abduction with intent to prevent liberation.

elements: Defendant intentionally damaged a building
By starting a fire or causing an explosion
When another person was present in the building and the defendant knew or had reason to know that fact
notes: First-degree arson requires knowledge of person in building. Second degree (§ 53a-112, Class B Felony) covers buildings without persons. Third degree (§ 53a-113, Class C Felony) covers property.

elements: Defendant with intent to cause the death of another person
Engaged in conduct constituting a substantial step toward the commission of murder
enhancements: Victim is a law enforcement officer
notes: Attempt to commit a Class A Felony is a Class B Felony. Assault in the first degree with intent to cause death may be charged instead.

statute_title: Assault in the First Degree — With Deadly Weapon
elements: Defendant with intent to cause serious physical injury
Caused serious physical injury to another person
By means of a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument
notes: 5-year mandatory minimum. Deadly weapon includes any firearm, knife, or instrument capable of causing death or serious physical injury.

offense_class: Class B Felony ($20,000+); Class C Felony ($10,000-$20,000); Class D Felony ($2,000-$10,000); Class A Misdemeanor ($500-$2,000); Class B Misdemeanor ($250-$500); Class C Misdemeanor (under $250)
penalty_max: 20 years (Class B); 10 years (Class C); 5 years (Class D); 1 year (Class A Misd.); 6 months (Class B Misd.); 3 months (Class C Misd.)
elements: Defendant committed larceny (§ 53a-119)
Obtained or withheld property from the owner by deception, embezzlement, false pretenses, extortion, or other unauthorized taking
enhancements: Theft from an elderly person (enhanced penalties)
notes: Connecticut uses 'larceny' as the general theft statute. Six degrees based on value. First degree ($20,000+) is a Class B Felony.

elements: Defendant committed larceny
Value of property or services exceeds $20,000
notes: Connecticut uses 'larceny' with degree-based value thresholds rather than 'grand theft' terminology.

elements: Defendant committed larceny
Value of property or services is under $250
notes: Under $250 is sixth-degree larceny, a Class C Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Same as larceny by value tier
penalty_max: Same as larceny by value tier
fine_max: Same as larceny by value tier
elements: Defendant concealed, removed, or altered merchandise
Of a retail establishment
With intent to deprive the merchant of value without paying
notes: Shoplifting is charged as larceny in Connecticut. Penalties follow the same degree/value structure.

elements: Defendant entered or remained unlawfully in a building
With intent to commit a crime therein
notes: Third-degree is the base burglary. Second degree (§ 53a-102, Class C Felony) involves dwelling or armed. First degree (§ 53a-101, Class B Felony) involves armed with explosives or deadly weapon in a dwelling.

elements: Defendant entered or remained unlawfully in a building
With intent to commit a crime therein
Defendant was armed with explosives or a deadly weapon
Or in the course of committing the offense, used or threatened use of physical force
notes: First-degree burglary is Class B Felony with 5-year mandatory minimum. Must involve a weapon or physical force in a building.

offense_class: Class D Felony (under $10,000); Class C Felony ($10,000-$20,000); Class B Felony ($20,000+)
elements: Defendant committed larceny of a motor vehicle
Without the owner's consent
notes: No separate motor vehicle theft statute. Charged as larceny based on value.

offense_class: Same as larceny by value tier
penalty_max: Same as larceny by value tier
fine_max: Same as larceny by value tier
elements: Defendant received, retained, or disposed of stolen property
Knowing that it was stolen or believing it was probably stolen
notes: Receiving stolen property is included under the general larceny statute § 53a-119(8). Degree determined by value.

statute_title: Criminal Mischief in the First Degree
offense_class: Class D Felony ($10,000+); Class A Misdemeanor ($1,000-$10,000); Class B Misdemeanor ($250-$1,000); Class C Misdemeanor (under $250)
elements: Defendant intentionally or recklessly damaged the property of another person
notes: Connecticut uses 'criminal mischief.' First degree covers $10,000+ damage. Four degrees based on damage amount.

statute_title: Criminal Trespass in the First Degree
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first degree); Class B Misdemeanor (second degree); Class C Misdemeanor (third degree)
elements: Defendant knowingly entered or remained unlawfully
In a building (first degree) or premises (second degree) or posted land (third degree)
notes: Three degrees. First degree (building) is Class A Misdemeanor. Third degree (posted land) is Class C Misdemeanor.

statute_title: Criminal Mischief in the First Degree
elements: Defendant intentionally damaged property of another
Damage exceeds $10,000
Or damage was by means of explosive
enhancements: Damage to utility or communication property
notes: First degree: $10,000+ or explosive. Second degree (§ 53a-116): $1,000-$10,000 (Class A Misdemeanor). Third degree (§ 53a-117): $250-$1,000 (Class B Misdemeanor).

statute_title: Family Violence — Assault, Threatening, or Harassment of a Family or Household Member
offense_class: Depends on underlying offense (assault, threatening, etc.)
elements: Defendant committed an act of family violence
Against a family or household member (spouse, former spouse, parent of common child, cohabitant, or dating partner)
Including assault, threatening, harassment, stalking, or sexual assault
notes: Connecticut addresses domestic violence through the family violence statute (§ 46b-38a). Not a standalone offense but triggers mandatory arrest, protective orders, and enhanced processing. Family Violence Education Program (diversionary) available for first offense.

offense_class: Class B Felony (first degree); Class D Felony (second degree); Class A Misdemeanor (third degree)
penalty_max: 20 years (first degree); 5 years (second degree); 1 year (third degree)
elements: Defendant caused physical injury to a family or household member
With the intent required for the applicable degree of assault
enhancements: Strangulation or suffocation (§ 53a-64bb, Class D Felony)
notes: Domestic battery charged as assault of the applicable degree with family violence designation triggering additional protections.

statute_title: Risk of Injury to a Minor
elements: Defendant willfully or unlawfully caused or permitted a child under 16
To be placed in a situation that its life or health was endangered
Or committed an act likely to impair the health or morals of a child under 16
mandatory_minimum: 1 year (not suspendable) if involving sexual contact
notes: Broadly applied statute covering various forms of child endangerment. One of the most commonly charged child-related offenses in Connecticut.

elements: Defendant was responsible for the care of a child under 19
Defendant intentionally maltreated, tortured, overworked, or cruelly punished the child
Causing physical harm or risk thereof
notes: Cruelty to persons statute covers child abuse. More serious injuries may also be charged under assault statutes. Mandatory reporting requirements apply.

elements: A valid protective or restraining order was in effect
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant willfully violated the order
enhancements: Violation involving physical contact or threat
notes: All violations of protective orders are Class D Felonies in Connecticut. Mandatory arrest upon violation.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (second degree); Class D Felony (first degree)
elements: Defendant knowingly engaged in a course of conduct directed at a specific person
That would cause a reasonable person to fear for their physical safety
Or suffer emotional distress
enhancements: Prior stalking conviction (first degree, Class D Felony)
Stalking in violation of court order (first degree)
notes: Second-degree stalking is Class A Misdemeanor. First degree (§ 53a-181c) is Class D Felony when done in violation of court order or with prior conviction.

offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor (second degree); Class D Felony (first degree)
elements: Defendant with intent to harass, annoy, or alarm another person
By telephone or electronic means communicated threats or obscenities
Or made repeated contacts to the other person
notes: Second-degree harassment covers most verbal/electronic harassment. First degree (§ 53a-182b) involves threats of physical contact or following.

statute_title: Abuse, Neglect, or Exploitation of an Elderly Person
offense_class: Class D Felony (abuse/neglect); Class B Felony (causing death)
elements: Defendant was responsible for the care of an elderly person (60+)
Defendant abused, neglected, or exploited such person
Resulting in harm to the elderly person's health or welfare
notes: Mandatory reporting under § 17b-451. Includes physical abuse, neglect, emotional abuse, and financial exploitation.

statute_title: Criminal Possession of a Firearm or Electronic Defense Weapon
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm
Defendant was a convicted felon, had been adjudicated delinquent for a serious juvenile offense, was subject to a protective order, or was otherwise prohibited
notes: 2-year mandatory minimum. Connecticut has strict gun laws. Permit required for handguns and most long guns.

statute_title: Criminal Possession of a Firearm — Convicted Felon
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm or electronic defense weapon
Defendant had previously been convicted of a felony
notes: 2-year mandatory minimum. Applies to all convicted felons. Connecticut also prohibits those convicted of certain misdemeanors from possessing firearms.

statute_title: Carrying a Pistol or Revolver Without a Permit
elements: Defendant carried a pistol or revolver
Upon the person or in a vehicle
Without a valid Connecticut pistol permit
notes: Connecticut requires a pistol permit for carrying. 1-year mandatory minimum. SB 1 (2023) aligned Connecticut with federal NYSRPA v. Bruen requirements.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (basic); Class D Felony (into dwelling)
elements: Defendant discharged a firearm
In a reckless or negligent manner
Creating risk of harm to persons or property
enhancements: Discharge into a dwelling (Class D Felony)
notes: Basic reckless discharge is a Class A Misdemeanor. Discharge into an occupied dwelling is a Class D Felony.

statute_title: Identity Theft in the Second Degree
offense_class: Class D Felony (second degree); Class B Felony (first degree, $10,000+); Class C Felony (third degree)
penalty_max: 5 years (second degree); 20 years (first degree); 10 years (third degree)
elements: Defendant knowingly used personal identifying information of another person
Without authorization
To obtain anything of value
notes: Three degrees based on value and circumstances. Mandatory restitution. Enhanced penalties for targeting elderly victims.

offense_class: Same as larceny by degree based on value
penalty_max: Same as larceny by value tier
fine_max: Same as larceny by value tier
elements: Defendant was entrusted with property of another
Defendant wrongfully took, obtained, or withheld the property
From the owner with intent to deprive
notes: Charged under the general larceny statute. Embezzlement is a theory of larceny under § 53a-119(1).

offense_class: Class D Felony (first degree); Class A Misdemeanor (second degree); Class B Misdemeanor (third degree)
penalty_max: 5 years (first degree); 1 year (second degree); 6 months (third degree)
elements: Defendant with intent to defraud, deceive, or injure
Falsely made, completed, or altered a written instrument
Which is or purports to be a government-issued document, deed, will, or financial instrument
notes: First degree covers government documents and financial instruments. Second degree (§ 53a-139) covers deeds, wills, and contracts. Third degree (§ 53a-140) covers other documents.

statute_title: Criminal Possession of a Forged Instrument in the First Degree
elements: Defendant possessed a forged instrument
Knowing it to be forged
With intent to defraud, deceive, or injure
notes: Counterfeiting of currency is primarily federal. State charges cover forged documents.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor ($250+); Class B Misdemeanor (under $250)
penalty_max: 1 year (Class A Misd.); 6 months (Class B Misd.)
elements: Defendant issued a check, draft, or order for payment
Knowing there were insufficient funds
With intent to defraud
notes: Defendant must have 10 days after notice to make good on the check before prosecution.

offense_class: Class D Felony (over $1,000); Class A Misdemeanor (under $1,000)
elements: Defendant knowingly and with intent to defraud
Presented or caused to be presented a false or fraudulent claim
To an insurance company
notes: Includes filing false claims, staged accidents, and arson-for-profit. Mandatory restitution.

offense_class: Same as larceny by value tier
penalty_max: Same as larceny by value tier
fine_max: Same as larceny by value tier
elements: Defendant used a credit card or debit card
Knowing it was stolen, forged, revoked, or canceled
To obtain goods, services, or anything of value
notes: Credit card fraud is classified using the same value tiers as larceny.

fine_max: $250,000 or twice the value of the property
elements: Defendant conducted or attempted to conduct a financial transaction
Involving proceeds of criminal activity
With knowledge that the property represents proceeds of criminal activity
With intent to promote the criminal activity or to conceal the source
notes: Class B Felony. Connecticut enacted money laundering provisions that align with federal statutes.

offense_class: Same as larceny by degree based on value
penalty_max: Same as larceny by value tier
fine_max: Same as larceny by value tier
elements: Defendant obtained property by creating or confirming a false impression
As to fact, value, intention, or law
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: General fraud charged as larceny by false pretenses under § 53a-119(2).

statute_title: Sexual Assault in the Second Degree
elements: Defendant compelled another person to submit to sexual contact
By use of force or threat of use of force against such person
Or the victim was physically helpless or mentally incapacitated
notes: Second-degree sexual assault covers non-penetration offenses by force. First degree (§ 53a-70) covers forcible penetration.

statute_title: Sexual Assault in the First Degree
offense_class: Class A Felony (aggravated); Class B Felony (basic)
elements: Defendant compelled another person to engage in sexual intercourse
By use of force or threat of use of force against such person
Or the victim was physically helpless or mentally incapacitated
mandatory_minimum: 10 years (aggravated, not suspendable); 5 years (basic, not suspendable)
enhancements: Use of a dangerous instrument (aggravated, Class A Felony)
notes: Connecticut uses 'sexual assault in the first degree' for what is commonly called rape. Aggravated sexual assault (§ 53a-70a) involving weapons, serious injury, or multiple perpetrators is Class A Felony. Sex offender registration required.

elements: Defendant performed an act of public indecency
Exposed private parts in a public place
With intent to arouse or gratify sexual desire, or to affront or alarm
notes: Class B Misdemeanor. Exposure to children may result in more serious charges under risk of injury to a minor (§ 53-21).

elements: Defendant engaged in or offered to engage in sexual conduct
In exchange for a fee
enhancements: Patronizing a minor for prostitution (§ 53a-83b, Class B Felony)
notes: Both the person offering and the patron can be charged. Patronizing a prostitute (§ 53a-83a) is a Class A Misdemeanor. Patronizing a minor is a Class B Felony.

statute_title: Possession of Child Pornography in the Second Degree
offense_class: Class D Felony (possession, second degree); Class C Felony (possession, first degree); Class B Felony (distribution); Class A Felony (production)
penalty_max: 5 years (second degree); 10 years (first degree); 20 years (distribution); 25 years (production)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed material depicting a minor engaged in sexually explicit conduct
Defendant knew the character and content of the material
notes: Federal charges are common. Sex offender registration required. First degree (§ 53a-196c) covers 50+ items.

statute_title: Failure to Register as a Sex Offender
elements: Defendant was required to register under the Sex Offender Registration Act
Defendant knowingly failed to register or update registration
notes: Must register within 3 days. Connecticut's Megan's Law requires registration and community notification.

statute_title: Sexual Assault in the Second Degree — Statutory
offense_class: Class C Felony (if 3+ years age difference); Class D Felony (if 2-3 years age difference)
elements: Defendant engaged in sexual intercourse with another person
Other person was 13-15 years old
Defendant was more than 2 years older than the victim
notes: Age of consent in Connecticut is 16. For victims aged 13-15, the offense requires a specified age difference. Sex offender registration required.

elements: Defendant with intent to cause inconvenience, annoyance, or alarm
Or recklessly creating a risk thereof
Engaged in fighting or violent, tumultuous, or threatening behavior
Or made unreasonable noise or obscene gestures
notes: Common add-on charge. Often paired with resisting arrest or breach of peace (§ 53a-181).

statute_title: Interfering with an Officer / Resisting Arrest
elements: Defendant obstructed, resisted, hindered, or endangered
Any peace officer or firefighter in the performance of their duties
notes: Connecticut uses 'interfering with an officer' which covers resisting arrest. Physical resistance causing injury may lead to additional assault charges.

elements: Defendant intentionally obstructed, impaired, or perverted
The administration of justice
notes: Covers tampering with witnesses, concealing evidence, and other interference with judicial proceedings.

offense_class: Varies (civil or criminal; summary or constructive)
elements: Defendant willfully disobeyed a lawful order of the court
Or engaged in disruptive behavior in the courtroom
Or failed to appear as ordered
notes: Criminal contempt is punitive; civil contempt is coercive. Right to jury trial for serious criminal contempt.

offense_class: Not a criminal offense in most circumstances
elements: Person appears in a public place
Under the influence of alcohol or drugs
To the degree that the person is incapacitated or a danger
notes: Connecticut does not have a general public intoxication crime. Intoxicated persons may be taken to a treatment facility. Disorderly conduct may apply if behavior is disruptive.

statute_title: Failure to Appear in the First Degree
offense_class: Class D Felony (first degree, felony case); Class A Misdemeanor (second degree, misdemeanor case)
elements: Defendant was released on bail or personal recognizance
Required to appear in connection with a charge of a felony
Defendant intentionally failed to appear
notes: First degree: FTA in a felony case (Class D Felony). Second degree (§ 53a-173): FTA in a misdemeanor case (Class A Misdemeanor). Bench warrant issued.

elements: Defendant reported false information to a law enforcement agency
Knowing the information was false
Regarding the alleged commission of a felony
notes: Filing a false report of a felony is Class A Misdemeanor. False report of a misdemeanor (§ 53a-180d) is Class B Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (second degree); Class D Felony (first degree)
elements: Defendant threatened to commit any crime of violence
With intent to terrorize another person
Or in reckless disregard of the risk of causing terror
enhancements: Threat to commit a crime of violence involving a deadly weapon (first degree, § 53a-61aa, Class D Felony)
notes: Second-degree threatening covers general threats. First degree (§ 53a-61aa) involves threats with deadly weapons.

elements: Defendant made a material false statement under oath
In an official proceeding
Defendant did not believe the statement to be true
notes: Perjury in any official proceeding is a Class D Felony. False statement (§ 53a-157b) covers other sworn statements.

elements: Defendant offered, conferred, or agreed to confer any benefit
Upon a public servant
With intent to influence the public servant's official action
notes: Both the giver and receiver can be charged. Receiving a bribe (§ 53a-147) is also a Class C Felony.

offense_class: Class C Felony (first degree); Class D Felony (second degree)
elements: Defendant escaped from custody
Using physical force or threat of physical force
Or from a correctional institution
notes: First degree involves use of force. Second degree (§ 53a-170) is escape without force.

offense_class: Class D Felony (intentional torture/killing); Class A Misdemeanor (other cruelty)
elements: Defendant unjustifiably injured, maimed, mutilated, or killed an animal
Or failed to provide proper food, drink, or shelter
enhancements: Intentional torture or malicious killing (Class D Felony)
notes: Intentional cruelty is a Class D Felony. Negligent cruelty is a Class A Misdemeanor. Animal fighting is separately classified.

penalty_max: Remaining suspended sentence on underlying offense
elements: Defendant was placed on probation
Defendant violated a condition of probation
Violation was willful
enhancements: New criminal offense while on probation
notes: Court may revoke, modify, or continue probation. Defendant entitled to a violation hearing. Standard of proof is preponderance of the evidence.

penalty_max: Remaining sentence or remaining special parole period
elements: Defendant was released on parole or special parole
Defendant violated a condition of parole
Violation was established at a revocation hearing
notes: Board of Pardons and Paroles makes revocation decisions. Connecticut has 'special parole' which is a defined post-incarceration supervision period that is part of the original sentence.

statute_title: Criminal Liability for Acts of Another
elements: Defendant solicited, requested, commanded, importune, or intentionally aided another person
To engage in conduct constituting an offense
With the mental state required for the commission of the offense
notes: A person is criminally liable for the conduct of another when they are an accomplice. Punishable to the same extent as the principal.

offense_class: One class below the attempted offense (attempt of Class A = Class B; etc.)
penalty_max: Varies — one class below the attempted offense
elements: Defendant acting with the kind of mental state required for commission of the crime
Intentionally engaged in conduct which would constitute the crime if attendant circumstances were as the defendant believed them to be
Intentionally did or omitted to do anything constituting a substantial step toward the commission
notes: Attempt reduces the offense classification by one level. Attempt to commit a Class A Felony is a Class B Felony.

offense_class: One class below the target offense
penalty_max: Varies — one class below the target offense
elements: Defendant with intent that conduct constituting a crime be performed
Agreed with one or more persons to engage in or cause the performance of such conduct
Any of them committed an overt act in pursuance of the conspiracy
notes: Conspiracy reduces the offense by one class level. Requires an overt act. Renunciation is a defense if defendant thwarts the success of the conspiracy.
